messages:
jia: FYI ran an experiment with speculative decode + int8-static on the new 13B variant. noticed a 'hesitation' pattern around punctuation: model outputs a burst of low-confidence tokens (commas/periods) then often emits EOS a few tokens later. anyone seen punctuation-triggered truncation before?
sam: interesting. can you paste an example? also what speculative config?
jia: example prompt: "Summarize the meeting notes: key decisions, next steps, owners." output truncated after a sentence ending with a period, e.g., "...assign follow-ups to the product lead." <EOS> even though the expected summary is longer. config: speculative size=3, accept_thresh=0.65, sampler top-p=0.9 temp=0.8, beamless. quant: int8 static with layerwise scale and outlier clamp.
leah: punctuation tokens often have sharp logit spikes; quant noise might push the dot token above threshold in stage1. speculative then accepts early. could also be tokenizer merges adding a trailing subtoken that looks like an end marker.
benchbot: run 3312345690 summary: p50=28ms p95=86ms speculative_accept=21% truncation_rate=0.038. artifacts: s3://bench/3312345690/trace.jsonl
sam: do we have per-token logit traces? compare stage1 vs stage2 EOS logit deltas for punctuated tokens. if deltas small -> accept was premature.
jia: grabbed a trace for one failed case: stage1 EOS logit=4.2, stage2 EOS logit=4.3 (delta 0.1). other high-likelihood tokens had >0.6 delta. looks like stage2 didn't change much.
leah: that delta small suggests quant induced correlated noise across stages (same prefetch path). we should force independent randomization between speculative and main decode or increase stage2 verification steps.
opsbot: suggestion: toggle speculative `verify_offline=true` to recompute logits in FP16 for stage2; cost+latency impact will be higher.
sam: can we instead add a small monotonic correction to punctuation logits in quant builds? e.g., a tiny bias to punctuation tokens to avoid spur EOS. risky but cheap to test.
jia: quick AB: add -0.5 bias to EOS token logits in quant builds -> truncation_rate drops to 0.012, but coverage of genuine short summaries falls by 0.9% (acceptable?).
leah: risky as a permanent hack. better to patch accept heuristic: require second-best gap > X when EOS is candidate. that would avoid single-token spikes.
benchbot: new run 3312345775 started: variant=13b-int8-spec-heuristic, sample=50k short-prompts, expected 3h. will post diff vs FP16 baseline.
sam: also add a short-prompt gating rule in rollout: for prompts predicted short (< 20 tokens), disable speculative or increase verification.
jia: adding to rollout checklist: 1) token-level trace collection for first 10k requests, 2) heuristic tweak (second-best gap), 3) AB on bias trick for quick signal, 4) log tokenizer mapping diff between trimmed vs full vocab. starting traces now.
leah: for eval harness, let's compute "truncation precision/recall" where precision = flagged truncations that are true truncations, recall = detected real truncations. need a small labeled set of 500 short-summary prompts. volunteers?
sam: i'll label 200, jia 200, leah 100.
opsbot: canary policy updated: speculative off for trimmed-vocab quant builds until heuristics validated. policy id: canary_spec_2026_03.
jia: thanks all. will post summary when benchbot returns. :sparkles:
